title: Select Sector indices — conditional quarter-end secondary reweighting (24%/4.8%/50% breach test), the year-end instance whose drift window is the LONGEST of the four quarters at eight full sessions
source: EST: rule-derived, not a scheduled publication. SEC EDGAR, Select Sector SPDR Trust Form 497, accession 0001193125-26-031948, document d85739d497.htm, RE-FETCHED DIRECT 2026-09-09 by this event's own initial research (HTTP 200, 2,388,335 bytes — byte-identical to the 2026-09-05, 2026-09-06, 2026-09-08 and 2026-09-09 sibling fetches, which is a cheap integrity check that no session read a mutated document) and re-parsed from raw HTML rather than inherited. Verbatim: "The rebalancing of the Select Sector Indices, based on the processes described above, occurs at the closing prices of the second Friday of March, June, September and December. Changes will become effective after the market close on the third Friday of March, June, September and December. Additionally, if, on the second to last business day of March, June, September, or December a company has a weight greater than 24% or the sum of the companies with weights greater than 4.8% exceeds 50%, a secondary reweighting will be triggered with the reweighting effective date being after the close of the last business day of the month." DECEMBER 2027 APPLIED, and the one load-bearing calendar question ANSWERED FROM THE PRIMARY rather than assumed: December 2027's Fridays are the 3rd, 10th, 17th, 24th and 31st, so the reference close is Fri 2027-12-10 and capping goes effective after the Fri 2027-12-17 close. Whether 2027-12-31 is the last business day turns entirely on whether the NYSE observes New Year's Day 2028 (a Saturday) on the preceding Friday — if it did, the test would be 2027-12-29 and this entry's date would be wrong. nyse.com/markets/hours-calendars, fetched direct 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200, 109,180 bytes) and parsed cell-by-cell, answers it VERBATIM in its own footnote: "Because the holiday falls on Saturday, January 1, 2028, no New Year's Day holiday is observed." So 2027-12-31 is a full equity session, the last business day of December 2027, and the breach test is struck on the Thu 2027-12-30 close. The same page's Christmas row reads "Friday, December 24 (Christmas Day observed)" for 2027 with NO early-close asterisk, and its **** footnote names Thursday, December 24, 2026 as the only December early close in the entire 2026-2028 table. Filed estimate because the trigger is CONDITIONAL — most quarters it does not fire and no primary source can pre-confirm that it will — and on the two standing counts this family records: the filing dates the RULE not this instance, and this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep. Checked 2026-09-09
notes: CANONICAL FILE written by this event's own never-assessed initial research (2026-09-09), which found the id existed only as proposals/sp-select-sector-secondary-reweight-2027-12-31.from-sp-rebalance-reference-close-2027-12-10.json; that proposal was read in full first and its findings are carried forward, not discarded. Ledger: docs/research/events/sp-select-sector-secondary-reweight-2027-12-31.md. A BACKSTOP, not a base case — the December-2027 analogue of the 2026-09-30, 2026-12-31, 2027-03-31 and 2027-06-30 entries, and the call is the same stand-aside. WHAT IS SPECIFIC TO THIS INSTANCE, MEASURED THIS SESSION RATHER THAN INHERITED, AND IT POINTS THE OPPOSITE WAY FROM THE 2026-12-31 SIBLING: (1) THE WINDOW IS THE LONGEST OF THE FOUR QUARTERS. From the 12-17 effective close to the 12-30 test the sessions are 12-20, 12-21, 12-22, 12-23, [12-24 CLOSED], 12-27, 12-28, 12-29, 12-30 — EIGHT, all full. December 2026's is seven of which one is a 1:00 p.m. half day (~6.5 trading days), so December 2027 carries ~23% more trading time in the identical mechanic. The cause is that Christmas-on-a-Saturday converts December's half day into a full Friday closure and removes the early close entirely. (2) THE BASE RATE THAT APPLIES IS 11.7%, NOT 10.3%. Unconditional overlapping windows on the +4.35% AMZN-vs-XLY threshold this family uses, 2016-09-12 to date: six-session 8.7% (219/2,505), seven-session 10.3% (258/2,504) — both reproducing the siblings to the tenth from an independently written pipeline — and EIGHT-session 11.7% (292/2,503), the figure December 2027 actually runs against. (3) THE 2026 SIBLING'S HEADLINE DOES NOT SURVIVE THE EXTRA SESSION. Its 0-of-11 December record is arithmetically correct and is about the 4-to-8-session ACTUAL alignments 2015-2025. Constraining overlapping eight-session windows to start 12-15..12-20 so they stay inside December gives 2 of 47 (4.3%) in the modern era — and BOTH clears are December 2025, at +5.00% (12-16 to 12-29) and +5.02% (12-17 to 12-30). The second of those is December 2027's exact alignment: last December's tape WOULD have cleared the threshold on this instance's calendar shape. (4) THE COMPRESSION MECHANISM IS A MODERN-ERA FEATURE WITH NO PRE-2015 COUNTERPART, which no sibling could see from a 2015 start. Daily AMZN-vs-XLY excess-return stdev over 12-20..12-30 against its own era: modern 1.066% vs 1.399% = ratio 0.762; pre-2015 3.592% vs 3.557% = ratio 1.010, i.e. no holiday compression at all. The re-breach haircut splits the same way (modern ratio 0.37, pre-2015 0.88). So the effect is a property of the modern AMZN/XLY pair, not of the December calendar, and its survival to 2027 is an assumption rather than a measurement — registered as a forward test rather than asserted. (5) THE EXACT CALENDAR TWINS ARE 2004, 2010 AND 2021 — the only other years with Dec 25 on a Saturday, hence the same eight-session window, full-Friday closure and trading 12-31. They printed +9.57%, +2.55% and −5.61%: ONE OF THREE cleared, and the one that did is the largest December print in the whole 26-year table. n=3, a list and never a rate. (6) THE FILING RISK THE PROPOSER FLAGGED IS RE-CHECKED AND ONE NEW DOCUMENT CLEARS IT: post-effective amendment 485APOS 0001193125-26-303372 (filed 2026-07-14, effective ~2026-09-27, deletes the capping methodology) is still the latest amendment on EDGAR as of 2026-09-09 — no 485BPOS — so sp-rebalance-reference-close-2027-12-10's FT-…-1 stays live; and the intervening 497 nobody had read, accession 0001193125-26-269239 filed 2026-06-12, is a 5,210-byte REDEMPTION-PROCEDURES supplement carrying zero occurrences of "second Friday", "Quarterly Qualification", "4.8%", "24%" or "Component Stock" — it does NOT supersede the January 497 for this rule. (7) THE CORRIDOR IS THE THINNEST THIS FAMILY HAS SEEN — four tracked entries within five days (29 around the September instance, 14 around the 2026 year-end one), and the FOMC minutes land the day BEFORE the test rather than on it as they do in 2026. The Russell family's own conditional year-end capping, which made the 2026 instance's "two index families recapping on one close" note, is NOT on the calendar for 2027-12-31 — proposed this session as proposals/russell-style-quarter-end-capping-effective-2027-12-31.from-sp-select-sector-secondary-reweight-2027-12-31.json. Honest caveats re-stated rather than laundered: issuer holdings weights are capped index weights drifted by price plus a cash residual, so every cohort sum is a floor on the float-adjusted index weights the test actually applies to, and an ETF relative return cannot adjudicate 24.00% from 24.06%. SIX capping resets stand between today and the 2027-12-17 reset, so no weight observable now survives to the test. Low impact and estimate status: it widens caution about the 2027-12-30 and 2027-12-31 closes and licenses nothing, and no house playbook (S1/S2/E1/S3/S4/G1) is index-flow-keyed (trade-playbooks.md and multi-symbol-sweep.md re-grepped 2026-09-09 for rebalanc|index effect|select sector|capping|secondary reweight — zero hits). Kind `sector` is the closest fit the enum offers for a market-structure flow event; the imperfect fit is named, not fixed from this lane.
